subject: Identify change points in a vector of count data

messages.author: 99dfe63dc70fad26
messages.subject: Identify change points in a vector of count data
parts:
I am relatively new to bayesian analysis and statistical modelling.  I am looking at count data and I would like to use an appropriate model to identify change points. You can imagine an indexed  vector of data for example c(0,0, 10,11,11,3,10,9,20,21,19,18,21). I would also like to identify hotspots (i.e. regions with relatively high count values). I imagine (stand  to be corrected) the count data  could be described by a Poisson distribution and that lambda oscillates between high and low values in the case of hot and cold spots or it remains constant.  I am interested in finding  the switch point positions or regions  where the value of the parameter lambda suddenly changes. 

Is this a valid way to look and answer the question, How would code this in stan language?

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: Identify change points in a vector of count data
parts:
Check out section 14.2 in the manual for an example of a change point model. You can find the data for that model here: https://pymc-devs.github.io/pymc/tutorial.html

You mention multiple change points; there's information on that in that section as well (search for "Multiple Change Points"). The multiple change point model is going to be more difficult than the single change point one though, so I'd start with the single change point model and see how it works for you before upping the complexity.

Ben
